If it is five days I guess that would be five months, five and a little months, but in any case we are considerably beyond six to nine weeks which was the belief of the Trial Chamber. Let me encourage the parties. You have worked I thought pretty well together or closely together pretrial. We had at least six or so status conferences. I would imagine there has been a sincere effort to provide the Defence with sufficient evidence, I mean, your exhibits and certainly the witness list. Have you attempted to reach any stipulations of fact regarding some of these witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We have ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have given the statements, all the statements of your witnesses you have given to the Defence, so it is not a matter of your hiding at least from the Defence. We have not received this of course and do not want it. You are not hiding it. So it seems to me the extent you can stipulate facts, stipulate perhaps as to what a witness might say, I am not suggesting that you not offer the witnesses's testimony because you certainly have the right to. I am just trying to encourage you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we only too pleased to be able to do that. It is a bit difficult for the Prosecution to go out and solicit stipulations from the Defence. If the Defence are willing to stipulate particular matters in the case, we are only too pleased to be able to take that on board and reduce the length of our case; we would very actively encourage that. But we are reluctant to put too much pressure on the Defence in that regard. If the Defence wish to come forward and discuss with us, we are only too willing and hopefully we can resolve it with stipulations if the Defence are so inclined. We have actually written to the Defence on one occasion about the possibility of a stipulation, but it is not something that we have ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can we be of assistance? I am sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It is not something we have been trying to pursue too vigorously. If the Defence come to us our doors are open and we are only too willing to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can I be the catalyst? I understand that that is the case sometimes and no one wants to take the first move. Suppose we take the first move and encourage the two of you to meet? Perhaps we can even have a status conference to facilitate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We would certainly welcome that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have provided Defence counsel with the witness list, not the order I gather?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And the order and the counts.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then you have provided, even though it was filed confidentially you have provided that. So they have then what we have?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we will set a status conference and see what we can do to encourage further stipulations, not to in any way cut you off because I understand the burden that you have, but to perhaps act as the catalyst to encourage the stipulations that can be made and take a close look at the witnesses who have been listed. I do not want you to think, though, that I am cutting you off; it is just that I was looking at six to nine weeks and Friday I just happened to at a moment in the testimony start fiddling with the numbers and I came up with 16 weeks, and I had difficulty sitting here at that point. Then when I found out it was even longer. I think that is probably what we will do. Judge Stephen is saying that as you have already seen, we do not have the exclusive use of this room. This Trial Chamber, Trial Chamber Two, will be meeting tomorrow in a matter that will be scheduled for trial perhaps right after this trial is completed, and there are two other matters that are pending before the other Trial Chamber. Am I correct? There are two indictments ----

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- where there have been initial appearances before the other Trial Chamber and they are waiting in line and, of course, as I have said, we have only one courtroom. It is very important for us to give as much time as necessary to this case and we will do that, but I just do not want to leave any stone unturned. So, I think maybe we will schedule a meeting where we can all sit and, as President Lyndon Johnson said, reason together. Maybe if we all sit and reason together we can shorten some of the testimony. But we do have another matter to consider in the morning, so we will adjourn until 2.30 tomorrow.

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
(The hearing adjourned until 2.30 p.m. the following day)
